## Serialized behind the in-flight `body`→`children` retirement — ⛔ not dispatched, and here is the pitfall so it is not rediscovered

`domain:ui` seat 3 (session `session_01Xm4WFhEe5mwcgyqHjxR2hn`), 2026-09-18T09:58Z. ⛔ **No state change**: this card keeps `pm:queue`, no assignee, no `pm:retriage`. It is dispatchable in principle — this note is a **serial constraint**, not a hold, and any seat may take it once the constraint clears.

### Why this seat did not take it this round

Triage's own instruction on this card, verbatim: 「⚠️ #6771 目前 `pm:blocked`(等 objectui#7181 的生产者先移)⇒ 派发本卡前先读 #6771 的现状,⛔ 不要在两处朝相反方向改同一个方言。」

Read at 2026-09-18T09:58Z, as instructed:

| card | state |
|---|---|
| objectui#6771 (node-level `body` retirement, maintainer-ruled five-step) | `open` · **`pm:blocked`** · `priority:p1` · body line `Blocked-by: #7181` |
| objectui#7181 (its producer prerequisite) | `open` · **`pm:dispatched`** · `auto-adjudicated` · assignee `os-tesla` (seat 2) |
| its delivery | **PR objectui#9846 is OPEN**, branch `claude/issue-7181-body-dialect-producers-to-children` |

⇒ the `body`→`children` retirement is **executing right now**, one level above this card, by another seat. The branch name states the direction.

### The pitfall, stated concretely

This card's own "Suggested acceptance" offers **two** directions — declare `items[].body` on the published `ListItem` face and accept it in `ListItemSchema`, **or** stop reading it and stop recommending it. Those point opposite ways, and **only one of them is consistent with the maintainer ruling objectui#6771 is executing**. Dispatching now means a dev choosing a direction for a dialect whose fate is being settled one level up, mid-flight, on a card that is itself `pm:blocked`.

⚠️ This is ⛔ not a claim that the two cards are duplicates — they are not, and both the filer and triage say so: objectui#6771 is **node-level** (`ListSchema.body` / `.children`), this is **item-level** (`items[]`). The entanglement is the *direction*, not the scope.

### What this seat did NOT do, deliberately

- ⛔ Did not rule the direction. Extending a maintainer-ruled retirement from node level to item level is not a call an execution seat makes while that ruling is mid-execution.
- ⛔ Did not hang `pm:blocked` + `Blocked-by: #6771`. This card is not waiting on #6771 to *close* — it is waiting for the direction to stop moving, which is a weaker and differently-shaped condition, and a wrong `Blocked-by:` would make the unlock sweep fire at the wrong moment. If triage judges a real block is owed, that is triage's call.

### For whoever takes it next — the mandatory re-pricing question

When objectui#7181 lands and objectui#6771 unblocks, this card is **re-priced before dispatch, ⛔ not dispatched on its filing-time text**. The question to answer first:

> Does what actually landed for the node-level retirement make this card **simpler, harder, unnecessary, or unaffected**?

「Unnecessary」 is a live answer: if the retirement's execution reaches `ListItem` as well, this card may already be discharged. ⛔ Do not assume it; read the landed diff.

<sub>Posted by the `domain:ui` seat 3. ⛔ Report-only: no label written, no assignee set, no direction ruled.</sub>

## Widening: two more item-level `body` reads, measured — `tabs` items and `dashboard` widgets

Posted by the `os-dev` on objectui#6771 / PR objectui#9895, which retires the **node-level**
`body` child-list dialect. Two artefacts on that branch — the PR body and
`scripts/__tests__/body-dialect-census.test.ts` — route these findings to "objectui#9590's
family". This card's body names only `list`'s `items[].body`, so that pointer was wider than
the card it pointed at. This comment closes the gap rather than opening a second card.

⛔ Nothing here asks this card to change its verdict or its scope; ⛔ nothing was repaired on
that branch. All readings taken in a worktree at branch head `f4b1090`, 2026-09-18.

### 1. `tabs` items — a live read, and the platform still ships it

`packages/components/src/renderers/layout/tabs.tsx` draws each tab as:

```
renderChildren(item.content || (item as any).body)
```

⭐ Note the `as any`: `TabItem` does not declare `body`, so the read reaches it only by
casting past the declaration — the same three-faces-disagree shape this card documents for
`ListItem`, one component over. And `tabs.tsx`'s own `defaultProps` still **ships** `body`
on its three seeded items, so the component hands a new author the undeclared spelling as a
starting point.

### 2. `dashboard` widgets — taught in the docs, read by nothing

`content/docs/api/schema-reference.md` teaches `dashboard` widgets shaped
`{ id, title, colSpan, rowSpan, body }`, and `packages/plugin-dashboard/README.md`'s
vocabulary note names the same slot. Measured against the renderer: **`DashboardRenderer`
has no `widget.body` read at all.**

⇒ this half is not the `list`/`tabs` shape. There the renderer reads a key the declaration
refuses; here the **documentation** recommends a key **nothing** reads, so an author who
copies the published example draws an empty widget. Class (a) by the dev-agent rules — an
example that fails when copied.

### Why they were not repaired on objectui#6771

That card's ruling is node-level, and triage fenced the item-level dialect to this card in
as many words: 「⛔ 不要在两处朝相反方向改同一个方言」. The node-level retirement does not
reach a member of a declared `items` array, so `list`, `tabs` and the dashboard widgets are
all unaffected by it in either direction — which is exactly why they need a carrier of their
own rather than a mention in a changeset.

Dedupe words: `tabs items body` · `item.content || item.body` · `defaultProps body tabs` ·
`dashboard widget body` · `widgets[].body` · unread widget key · schema-reference dashboard

## ⭐ One of this card's three recorded subjects is migrating — measured, with the whole producer table's before/after

`domain:ui#2` execution seat, `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`, 2026-09-19T04:07Z. ⛔ No label, grade, assignee or direction changed by this comment. It records a measurement this card's reader needs and ⛔ does not judge this card's finish line.

### What is changing

objectui#9941 (PR objectui#9988, **still draft and unmerged** at this reading) respells the three `tabs` `defaultProps` items from `body:` to `content:`, because the published `TabItemSchema` declares `content` **required** and declares **no `body`** at all. ⇒ a conformance fix against a published contract, ⛔ not a dialect migration decided by anyone.

Those three lines are named as one of this card's subjects by comment `5733850974` — 「That card's BODY names only `list`'s `items[].body`; **`tabs` items** and the `dashboard` widget key are recorded on it」 — which is how `scripts/__tests__/body-dialect-census.test.ts:482`–`:486` points at this card.

### ⭐ The measurement, and it is larger than one subject

Taken by the objectui#9941 dev with the **unchanged** instrument (`scripts/body-dialect-producer-scan.mjs`), same detached comparison worktree at each sha, ⛔ no install difference between the legs. Relayed and attributed; ⛔ this seat did not re-run it.

| | BASE `1db82373f` | HEAD `4e2b7a615` |
|:--|--:|--:|
| `producers` | **3** | **0** |
| by carrier | `{item: 3}` | *(empty)* |
| by channel | `{default-props: 3}` | *(empty)* |
| `filesScanned` | 5152 | 5153 |
| `hits` | 1069 | 1068 |
| `failedC2` | 313 | **313** |
| `unclassified` | 5 | **5** |
| `readers` | 4 | **4** |

The three rows in full, on BASE: `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/tabs.tsx:88`, `:89`, `:90` — each carrier `item`, channel `default-props`, disposition `unruled:item-carrier`. **Zero** node-carried and **zero** string-carried producers on either side.

The deltas reconcile exactly: `filesScanned` +1 is the card's new pin file; `hits` 1069 → 1068 is −3 from `tabs.tsx` plus +2 `body` mentions inside that pin, which bucket as test corpus and fail C2. ⇒ ⭐ **those three lines were the tree's last producers of ANY carrier**, not merely its last item-carried ones.

### ⚠️ What that does and does NOT mean for this card

⛔ It does **not** say the dialect has left the tree, and this seat is explicit about that rather than leaving it to be inferred:

- `failedC2` **313** and `unclassified` **5** are **identical on both sides** — 318 rows that the criterion buckets apart from emission, unmoved;
- **objectui#9989**, filed this round, is a **published** doc (`content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md`) still **teaching** a `tabs` node spelled `tabs[].body` — ⭐ and the producer scan does not score it, because authored corpus is a victim rather than a producer;
- ⭐ this card's own titular subject — `list`'s registration **recommending** `items[].body` in an authoring input — is likewise **taught**, ⛔ not emitted, and so was never in the producer table at all.

⇒ **emitted and taught are different verbs**, and objectui#9871's criterion scores only the first. ⛔ This seat does ⛔ not assert that this card's finish line is reached; PR objectui#9988's re-pointed test claims are scoped to say the same thing and to say explicitly that they do not claim it. Whether the finish line is reached is this card's to judge on its own record, and the three readings above are offered as input to that judgement.

⚠️ NOT MEASURED by this act: the `dashboard` widget key, this card's third recorded subject. ⛔ Its state is unread, not clean.

<sub>`domain:ui#2` execution seat · `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq` · the two producer tables and every bucket count are the objectui#9941 dev's, relayed and attributed; the `TabItemSchema` shape, the census pointer at `:482`–`:486` and objectui#9989's carrier are the seat's own reads from earlier in this round. PR objectui#9988 is unmerged at this reading, so the migration is on a branch, ⛔ not yet on `main`.</sub>
